title: A task-dispatch controller carries the auth check per-action, and one task was written without it — with no upload type allow-list behind it
index_line: T-0030 · FILE_WRITE · an anonymously reachable controller task writes an attacker-typed file under the web root · php/any-task-dispatch · corroborated
invariant_violated: Authorization is assumed to be a property of the *component*, enforced once at the front of its controller, so individual tasks only need to do their job. Where the controller dispatches to tasks and the check lives in each task, the one task written without it is anonymously reachable — and an upload handler with no extension allow-list turns that reachability into code on disk.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated request names a component and one of its tasks in the query string
the component's controller resolves the task name and dispatches straight to it — the permission check is each task's own responsibility
the chosen task is an editor convenience (upload a custom icon) and it performs no access check at all, so the request proceeds as an anonymous user
the uploaded file is written to a folder under the web root with its original extension, because the platform's own upload-validation helpers were not called
the attacker requests the written file, and the web server executes it in the application's context

source.http.request.value: the `option`/`task` pair plus a multipart body — one request to upload, one to trigger; no session, no CSRF token, no login

sink.file.write.value: the upload move/save into a web-reachable directory; the extension and the destination are the two things to check

guard.none.value: no per-task access check and no extension allow-list — the two missing controls are independent, and either alone would have stopped it

encoding.path.value: the filename/extension, plus any sub-path the task accepts for the destination

preconditions.expr: the component exposes task-style dispatch and at least one task performs a file write
the upload task does not consult the platform's upload validator (extension allow-list / MIME check)
uploaded files land in a directory the web server executes (not a no-exec or off-root location)

check.spec: find . -path '*/images/*' -o -path '*/media/*' | head; grep -RniE 'php_flag engine off|RemoveHandler' images/ media/ 2>/dev/null | head

preconditions.expr: the component version predates the fixed release

success: an anonymous POST to the task returns success, and a GET to the written path returns executed output (not source)
the file keeps the extension the attacker chose — no rename, no forced image type
the response to the trigger request proves execution in the app's context, not a proxy error page
failure_like: the task is behind a token/permission check (the fix) and answers 401/403
the platform's upload validator is called, so only image extensions survive
the destination directory has execution disabled
false_positive: a 200 from the upload with the file stored as `.php.txt` or in a no-exec directory — check the stored name and the directory's handler config
the component being unpublished: the task may still be reachable if the component's controller is loaded
a shell that runs only because the attacker was already admin — this record's value is the *anonymous* reachability

hazards: component-task dispatch is the classic 'auth per action' anti-pattern: enumerate the task map and diff which tasks check and which do not — that diff is the finding
unpublishing a component does not remove its controller; a reachable task is reachable regardless of the UI
the two missing controls (auth and type) are independent — reporting only one understates the fix required
after exploitation the payload usually plants a second, durable admin; hunt for the persistence, not just the shell
non_transfers: frameworks whose dispatcher enforces a permission map before any task runs
upload paths that always re-encode the file (image resamplers) or rename to a fixed extension

evidence.target: SP Page Builder <= 6.6.1 for Joomla (CVE-2026-48908); fixed 6.6.2

provenance.author: mySites.guru responsible-disclosure write-up (CVE-2026-48908)
provenance.corroborates: the task name, the missing access check, the missing allow-list, the post-exploitation artefacts, and the fix's shape (auth + CSRF before every task)

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: 'unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files, ultimately resulting in the upload and execution of PHP code'; CWE-434; CVSS 3.1 9.8
